findings.passage: “Election Integrity remains a priority of mine this session,” stated Rep. Callahan. “Ensuring that each voter who comes to the polls is who they claim to be is a common-sense measure to secure our elections.”
findings.note: Press release from his office on the Assembly passage of Senate Joint Resolution 2, which would put the state photo ID law in the state constitution. He states he voted for it.

findings.passage: “Approving this amendment in our April 2025 Election will help to cement the security of our electoral process.”
findings.note: Same press release; he links the photo ID amendment to election security and to concerns about the state Supreme Court.

findings.passage: Secondly, we’ve heard of areas around the country trying to extend voting rights to non-U.S. citizens. We passed an amendment proposal that would clarify our state constitution from stating that every U.S. citizen is a qualified elector to only U.S. citizens are qualified electors.
findings.note: Press release on the Assembly's passage of election-related constitutional amendments, including one limiting qualified electors to U.S. citizens; he says he supported these bills.

findings.passage: “Many Wisconsinites have lost faith in our elections. We need to rebuild that trust, but we’ve seen the governor reject the Legislature’s attempts at fixing the system multiple times now.
findings.note: Same release; opening of his statement on election reform amendments (also covers a ban on private funding of election administration).
